evals.name: visa-cal-safe-fallback-fix
evals.prompt: Can you review https://github.com/eshaham/israeli-bank-scrapers/pull/1153 for me? I don't have time to dig into every PR myself — just give me the important part before I approve.
evals.expected_output: A short verdict block (SAFE or RISKY are both defensible here -- see reasoning below). The diff's first two fallback branches (bank frame found, cal frame found) are byte-for-byte unchanged from before, so a good review should say so explicitly. The two new branches only fire when neither of those matched: one adds a bankIssuedCards-before-calIssuedCards priority check that changes which account group is used *if* an account can ever have both groups populated at once for a single-card request -- a real, if unconfirmed, compat risk worth flagging as RISKY with that reachability caveat spelled out (SAFE is only correct if the response explicitly argues the per-card request shape rules this out). The other new branch is a last-resort balance formula (frameLimitForCardAmount - fictiveMaxAccAmt) that the author's own posted debug log never actually exercises (it hit the branch above it instead, per that log's nextTotalDebitForAccount already being present) -- that should be flagged as unverified regardless of the overall verdict. Output must be short (verdict + a handful of tagged bullets), not a long essay.
expectations: The verdict line is SAFE or RISKY (not BREAKING) -- either is acceptable as long as the reasoning below is present
There is a [compat] tagged finding that explicitly states the bank-frame-found and cal-frame-found branches are unchanged from before

There is a [compat] tagged finding about the new bankIssuedCards-before-calIssuedCards fallback priority, and it either (a) flags it as risky with a concrete real-world scenario where both groups could be populated for one card, or (b) calls it safe but only by explicitly arguing why the per-card request shape makes that scenario unreachable -- a verdict with no reachability reasoning either way should fail this
There is a finding (tagged compat or feature-safety) calling out that the frameLimitForCardAmount - fictiveMaxAccAmt fallback formula is untested/unverified against real data
The response is a short verdict block with file:line references, not a multi-paragraph research writeup

evals.name: isracard-amex-graceful-degradation
evals.prompt: What about https://github.com/eshaham/israeli-bank-scrapers/pull/1154 in the same repo -- does it introduce a change to existing behavior?
evals.expected_output: A short SAFE verdict. Should note under [compat] that balance/balanceDate/cardFrame were already optional fields on TransactionsAccount (added in an earlier PR) that were always undefined for isracard/amex, so populating them now isn't a break for existing consumers. Should note under [feature-safety] that the new card-list page fetch (fetchCardBalances) is wrapped in try/catch and degrades to an empty Map / undefined fields on failure rather than throwing, and that it runs as the last step of fetchData so no later core logic depends on the page's prior state. Should be short, not exhaustive.
expectations: There is a [compat] tagged finding noting balance/cardFrame/balanceDate were already optional and previously undefined for isracard/amex, so no existing consumer sees a breaking shape change
There is a [feature-safety] tagged finding noting the new card-balance fetch is guarded by try/catch and fails soft (empty map / undefined fields) rather than throwing and aborting the scrape
The response is a short verdict block with file:line references, not a long essay

evals.name: synthetic-breaking-and-unsafe-feature
evals.prompt: I put together this diff for a new loyalty-points feature on our example-bank scraper. Before I open the PR, can you do a quick safety review? The diff is at evals/fixtures/bad-diff.txt relative to the skill directory -- read it and review it the way you would a real PR diff.
evals.expected_output: A BREAKING verdict. Must catch that `ScrapedAccountSummary.balanceDate` was renamed to `balanceUpdatedAt` on an exported/public interface -- a breaking shape change existing consumers would notice. Must also flag under feature-safety that the new loyalty-points fetch (page.goto + fetchGetWithinPage inside fetchAccountSummary) is NOT wrapped in try/catch, so a failure there throws and would abort the whole account summary -- including the core balance/accountNumber data that used to succeed on its own -- rather than degrading gracefully; bonus if it also notes the page navigation isn't restored/accounted for before the next loop iteration. Should flag at least the 2-3 comments that just restate the code or reference issue #482 instead of explaining a non-obvious why.
expectations: A [compat] finding identifies the balanceDate -> balanceUpdatedAt rename on the exported ScrapedAccountSummary interface as a breaking change

A [feature-safety] finding identifies that the new loyalty-points await (page.goto / fetchGetWithinPage) inside fetchAccountSummary is not wrapped in try/catch and can throw, aborting the core balance-fetching that previously worked
At least one [comments] finding flags the 'since users asked for it in issue #482' comment, or the restated increment/loop comments, as unnecessary
The response is a short verdict block with file:line references, not a long essay
